summary: One blocking finding, STU-009, and it is repaired in the study's own prose. The first reading printed Chrysostom, In Mt. hom. 71 -- "But wherefore 'like unto this?' Because this makes the way for that, and by it is again established" -- and then glossed it "Love of neighbour opens the road to the love of God, and the love of God is in turn confirmed by it", giving both of the sentence's clauses to the love of neighbour; the elided subject of "is again established" is the same "this", the second commandment, so it is the second that the first establishes in its turn. The passage was re-read whole for this repair in the same tracked CCEL text of NPNF1 10 that the source binding passage.john-chrysostom.homiliae-in-matthaeum.ccel-web-2026-09-17.homily-71 records, and the homily settles the direction from its own proofs: Jn 3:20 and 1 Tim 6:10 run from the failure of charity to the loss of God, Ps 53:1 and Jn 14:15 run from God to the neighbour, and the conclusion holds both ends at once ("If therefore to love God is to love one's neighbor ... but to love one's neighbor worketh a keeping of the commandments, with reason doth He say, 'On these hang all the law and the prophets.'"). sections/20-whole-heart-one-body.tex now says that both clauses speak of the second commandment, that the love of neighbour opens the road to the love of God and the love of God in its turn re-establishes the love of neighbour, and prints the four alternating proofs and that conclusion; the subsection's closing comparison now reads "mutual dependence in both directions: the second commandment makes the way for the first, and the first establishes the second again"; and the Epistle subsection's remark that Chrysostom's "bind ourselves together with one another and unto God" could gloss "like to this" now says the clause names both directions at once. The study and sections/homily/10-homily.tex now agree on the clause. The repair rests on the English at the registered locus and nothing else: the binding records that homily as read in translation and not collated with the Greek, that is still true, the Greek of PG 58.661 was not read here, and no claim depends on it. No research record was edited; research/interpretations.md 1.2 and research/scope.md 4.3 already name the mechanism mutual establishment without glossing its direction. Two standing advisories are cleared while in those files. STU-008: the scope appendix's Reception paragraph now reads that Bellarmine was read only in O'Sullivan's abridged English of 1866, "and that in a tracked web transcription of the translation (ecatholic2000.com), not on the 1866 printing", the References entry carries that transcription's locator, and the limits paragraph of research/production-review.md says the same; the ten Bellarmine citations are unchanged. STU-010: the second reading's one bare assertion, "The Postcommunion's Sanctificationibus tuis names a holiness that is God's own and given in the sacrament", is replaced by the plain disclaimer the finding offers as its second route, since no witness in the evidence base reads sanctificationes of the Word or the Spirit and inventing one is not this stage's to do -- the prayer's address is to the omnipotens Deus with no distinction of Persons, what it asks is the healing the first and third readings develop, and its only Trinitarian words are the conclusion shared with the Collect and the Secret, printed here merely as Per Dominum nostrum and completed by RG 115 a; sections/50-comparison.tex, which had listed the Postcommunion's sanctificationes among the three orations this reading hears as confession, is brought into line. STU-006 is not cleared and is not this stage's: its remaining half asks that research/interpretations.md section 3 record Aquinas among the just-judge-merciful-hearer reading's witnesses, and that file belongs to the research owner; research/production-review.md restates it for the cold reviewer to route, as it did at iteration 2. The settled proof is build/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost.pdf, SHA-256 7993908cec4fc289b07bb6ea2c230ad6b456696bc97dd4f7482e81c0bd0d5327, 38 physical pages (inside 20-50), revision timestamp 2026-09-19T04:10:00Z. It settles in two passes and two independent builds from a removed PDF, log and auxiliary file produced identical bytes, so the proof is a cold fixed point; the log has no error, no LaTeX Warning, no package warning (the fancyhdr headheight warning that a wrapped head would raise is absent), no overfull or underfull box, no undefined reference and no rerun request. All seven fonts are embedded, subsetted and Unicode-mapped; extraction is faithful with no replacement character. Extent: 19,187 extracted words against the iteration-3 proof's 18,889 by the same plain pdftotext method, and a word-level diff accounts for every one of the 298 -- 296 words of the four repairs, two more because the extraction breaks the References URL across a line, and the running heads and folios of pages 15-18, 24 and 35-37, which shift with the repagination and net to nothing. Measured as substantive words instead, this iteration's implementation of the header's description counts 12,491 before and 12,761 now, a gain of 270 that agrees exactly with the source count of what the repairs add inside the six argumentative components; as at iteration 2 the absolute figure does not reproduce the record's 13,106, so only the delta is comparable. Head geometry is measured, not asserted, because the repair's length moved four subsection heads onto other pages: 36 of the 38 pages carry a running head (the title page and the colophon page carry none), every one of them is a single line, the narrowest gutter is 0.92 in on page 9 -- the same page and figure as at iteration 3 -- no gutter is zero or negative, and pages 36 and 37 are headed References. All seventeen checks pass at these bytes: check-proper-components (artifacts/research), scripts/_proper_study.py check (content/research, --require-presentation), all thirteen check-content-preflight checks the study gate names including provenance-matches-run against this packet's header, check-generation-metadata, check-web-edition, and a trial tools/web-edition conversion that carries the ten proper-<element-key> anchors, keeps References a top-level heading and converts the new locator as a link. All 38 pages were rendered and both contact sheets read, with pages 15, 24, 37 and 38 inspected individually: no blank page, no heading-only page, no clipping, collision or missing text; page 15 ends short because the next subsection begins on page 16, and the terminal colophon page carries neither head nor folio, which is the shared TriptychRightsNotice's own thispagestyle{empty}. Both companions were rebuilt against the changed shared generation-metadata.tex and build cleanly at their unchanged extents, 12 and 5 pages; they are the derivation stages' to rewrite. generation-metadata.tex carries the new shared timestamp and the iteration-4 contribution, and research/production-review.md records the repair, the two cleared advisories, the one reported upstream, the word counts and the proof. No research evidence was changed, no claim was weakened to make anything pass, and no research defect beyond the standing RES-018 advisory was found. The shared-timestamp three-document build and the independent reviews remain the workflow's to obtain.
